message: Our assembly line can only start a production run when parts from all three of our suppliers have arrived. Each supplier independently delivers on time 90% of the time. Our operations director said in the review, with total confidence: "Every supplier is 90% reliable, so we start on time 90% of the time. That's the number we'll quote to the customer." It sounds right to me; they're all at 90%, so the whole chain is at 90%. Can we quote 90% on-time starts to the customer?
response:
No, 90% isn't right. Because all three suppliers must deliver, the chain's reliability is the product of the individual probabilities (assuming they're independent, as you said):

0.9 × 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.729

So you'd start on time about **72.9%** of the time, roughly 73%, not 90%.

**Why the director's logic fails:** 90% would be right only if you needed just one supplier, or if the three were perfectly correlated (they all succeed or fail together). With three independent suppliers who are all required, each one is another chance for a delay, and the failures compound. Roughly 27% of runs will be held up by at least one late supplier, versus the 10% implied by the director's number.

**What to do:**
- Quote about 73% if the figure is based on supplier delivery alone. If you want to be a bit conservative, say "roughly 70%."
- Check the independence assumption. If the suppliers share a common risk (same shipping carrier, same region, weather), failures are correlated and the real number could be somewhat higher than 73%, but you'd need data to show that. Without it, 73% is the defensible figure.
- Check what "on time" means. The 90% is for each supplier's delivery, but a production start also depends on other things (staffing, equipment, and so on). If those can cause delays, the overall number will be lower still.
- If the customer needs a better number, the levers are buffer stock, earlier order lead times, or improving the weakest supplier. For example, raising each supplier to 95% gets you to about 85.7%, and to reach 90% overall you'd need each at roughly 96.5%.
